comment: The vectors pinning Prima.HostAPI as it crosses HTTP (Prima.WorkerWire): every call a runner makes and the report a worker service makes, sealed and signed with the keys of tests/fixtures/worker_auth.json, whose values keys repeats (root_hex is the root every other key derives from). Every consumer reproduces each call from its fields: body is the request body Prima.WorkerWire.request_body/2 writes, sealed as body_sealed in the body direction under the attempt seal key with body_iv_hex (Prima.WorkerAuth.seal_call/5); header is the host-call header over body_sealed, the bytes posted, under the attempt call key; answer is the answer written for it, sealed as answer_sealed in the answer direction with answer_iv_hex. Every body and answer carries v, the wire version, as its first member; a body whose v is absent or not version is unknown_version after it is opened and before its op is read, and an answer without it, or at another, is a lost answer. refusals are the plain answers each call may be given instead, with why. pre_body_refusals are headers a listener refuses before it reads a body, at now, for the member at standing, each answered at status with the refusal error names, in the order Prima.WorkerAuth documents: a version token other than v1, a header that does not parse, a timestamp outside window_ms, a MAC that is not the call key's, another generation, another member at the same generation, and a nonce the storage call (never retried) already presented for its attempt within the window. body_refusals are opened bodies posted at the renew route, refused with error. report is a worker service's runner_exited, plain under its dispatch key, answered plain; its cross_member names another member than the verifying one and is refused with error. retry_identity is one admit_child body sent twice, each time sealed and signed afresh under a new timestamp and nonce: the body, and so its child_key, is the same. connection_cases are admit_child calls under one attempt, in order, each answered as CYFR answers it for an attempt whose edge to the reference binds no named account: omitted names no connection and is admitted, its answer holding the child's assignment and in it the child's authority as the host answers it; named names the account Work, which the edge does not bind, and is refused connection_not_granted, setup required, with no default used in its place; reused repeats omitted's child_key naming Work, and is refused invalid_request before anything is answered from that key's child, since a key names one child and the connection it was admitted with. egress_pin_cases are egress_pin calls by name, answered with a Prima.PinnedTarget (id, ip, family, scheme, port, host, expires_at) or refused as Prima.PinnedTarget.refusals/0 names; a redirect names the pin its hop came from as from. egress_policy_cases are egress_pin calls in the order one attempt makes them, under an authority whose egress.domains is domains, each answered as an egress_pin case is; expect names whether the URL's host matches domains (domain_allowed, Prima.Network.domain_allowed?/2) and, for a redirect, whether its URL has the origin of the URL whose pin it names as from (same_origin, Prima.Network.same_origin?/2: scheme, host and effective port). A pin is answered only where both hold; a first request outside domains is denied and a hop to another origin is redirect_credentials. headers_before are a hop's request headers as [name, value] pairs, and headers_after are what a hop to another origin keeps of them (Prima.Network.strip_credentials/1). attached_fetch is the one call whose success is no single answer: posted with a Prima.AttachedRequest naming the runner's call_id, it is refused before admission by an ordinary sealed answer, a guest_error whose call_id is the request's (its refusals, each sealed with answer_iv_hex as answer_sealed), and admitted it is answered with frames, so the call carries no answer and the frames are frame_cases. A frame is a 4-byte big-endian length, one kind byte in clear (h head, c chunk, e end, x error) and the sealed value: Prima.MacEnvelope's seal of the plaintext under the attempt seal key, label cyfr-opus/v1/frame-answer, fields call_id, seq and kind (Prima.WorkerAuth.seal_frame/7). Each case's frames are read in order by a reader for call_id, one frame at a time; sealed_for says what a frame was sealed as (its call_id, seq, kind, iv_hex and plaintext_b64), tampered_from what a changed frame was sealed as before it changed, and expect the frames read (a head's status and headers, a chunk's body_b64, an end, an error's type and message) and the refusal that ends the answer, or null. egress_pin_internal_purposes are egress_pin calls naming a purpose CYFR alone takes (attached), each refused malformed. framing_headers and override_headers are the lowercase names, in order, of the headers an attached request may not set and an attach rule may not name: those that route or frame a request (Prima.Network.framing_headers/0) and those that override its method or target or claim a forwarded origin (Prima.Network.override_headers/0); a request setting one, in any case, is refused invalid_request naming it as spelled.

cases.name: head_chunk_end
cases.why: a well-formed answer: its head, one chunk and its end

cases.name: head_end
cases.why: an empty body: the end follows the head directly

read.message: The upstream did not answer in time.

cases.name: error_after_head
cases.why: an answer that failed after its head was sent ends as an error frame

read.message: The upstream did not answer in time.

cases.name: error_first
cases.why: an answer that failed before any head is one error frame at seq 0

cases.name: out_of_sequence
cases.why: a chunk sealed for seq 2 arriving at seq 1 does not open there

cases.name: chunk_first
cases.why: seq 0 is a head or an error, never a chunk

cases.name: another_call
cases.why: a frame sealed for another call id does not open as this call's

cases.name: bad_tag
cases.why: a sealed value changed in transit does not open

cases.name: kind_byte_changed
cases.why: a head whose clear kind byte was changed to an error's does not open: the kind is bound

cases.name: unknown_kind
cases.why: a kind byte other than h, c, e and x

cases.name: oversize
cases.why: a length above the frame bound, refused as soon as the length is in
